# Koushik Kotamraju

> Cloud security engineer building AI-native security platforms — production agentic systems, not prototypes. 9 years across detection engineering, IAM privilege analysis and identity governance, and multi-agent orchestration at enterprise scale. Open to Staff / Principal Cloud Security and AI Security roles. Portfolio: koushik.io

## Current Role

Senior Technical Security Engineer at Yahoo (Feb 2022 – present). Member of a small senior cloud security team (Paranoids) securing 2,800+ accounts across AWS and GCP, spanning every Yahoo business unit.

## Key Technical Achievements

**Secure-by-Default Guardrails & Detection Engineering**
Defines and operates Yahoo's company-wide cloud security baselines. Owns the AWS Cloud Alerts Detection system: 200+ active Python/Lambda detection signatures evaluating resource configurations across 1,400+ AWS accounts, producing per-resource findings and the account/BU/org security-posture scores (CSPM) the company is measured against — each with CIS-style audit and remediation guidance, deployed via Terraform. Primary point of contact for the AWS security baselines program: coordinated the program's largest control expansion (50+ new baselines) with Checkov parity analysis and risk × likelihood × impact severity re-scoring, grounded in a MITRE ATT&CK gap analysis against real-world attack techniques from cloud incident response data. Built the organization's first GenAI security capability from zero prior art — the first AI-service guardrails (Amazon Bedrock, SageMaker), the first GenAI detection signatures, and the usage governance that gated company-wide GenAI adoption.

**Posture Management & Security Metrics**
Designed and launched the org-wide High Severity Alert Enforcement Program — converted untracked critical cloud alerts into SLA-driven remediation tickets across the AWS estate and defined the posture metrics leadership uses to track risk burn-down. Presented the framework as an internal technical talk to engineers across the company, one of four such talks between 2023 and 2025.

**IAM Privilege Escalation Detection & Identity Governance**
Built an AI-native IAM audit agent organised around 10 vulnerability classes: critically permissive policies, role assumption chains, compute-to-data escalation, unused access, long-lived credentials, cross-account confused deputy, federated trust misconfiguration, identity persistence mechanisms, AI/ML service escalation, and logging and monitoring evasion indicators. Findings are matched against pathfinding.cloud, DataDog's public catalogue of 65+ documented escalation paths; that catalogue is theirs, the taxonomy and the semantic analysis layer are his. Combines static IAM policy graph analysis with LLM semantic interpretation to catch transitive permission chains and policy conditions rule-based tools miss. Built the GOAT benchmark first — 11 synthetic Terraform fixtures with 32 ground-truth findings — and evaluated the agent against all 32 before trusting it. Distributed org-wide via the internal security marketplace. Also built a toxic-combination correlation engine over CIS-based alert data, chaining findings into privilege-escalation paths across three classes (misconfig+misconfig, misconfig+IAM, IAM+IAM) — catching chains single-finding scanners miss.

**Antitoxin — CIEM Research**
A CIEM research and design project (Cloud Infrastructure Entitlement Management). Research and design stage: no implementation yet. 62 toxic IAM combinations catalogued by hand across 8 attack categories, each mapped to MITRE ATT&CK and each carrying a manually determined keystone permission whose removal breaks that chain. The catalogue is a draft pending citation re-verification. The tool boundary was drawn before any code existed: Antitoxin retains granted-versus-used correlation, catalogue synthesis, and alert-to-trust-policy validation, and delegates asset resolution and escalation-path analysis to systems that already own them.

**Artemis: Attack-Path Operationalization (GCP built, AWS designed)**
An operationalization layer over a native cloud security platform's attack-path analysis, which computes the highest-signal data available and exposes it only through a console: no structured export, no cross-finding correlation, and no history past the retention window. Implemented on GCP at an initial release: Security Command Center export, AI enrichment, business-context mapping, longitudinal tracking, dashboards (BigQuery, Vertex AI/Gemini, Terraform), and a coverage rotation that cycles resources through the platform's hard cap on how many can be designated for simulation at once. The AWS side is designed but not built: an architecture, a written gap analysis of that platform's exposure findings, and a roadmap phase. The unified cross-cloud view depends on the unbuilt side and does not exist yet. The written risk analysis names its own obsolescence condition, which is the vendor raising the limit the rotation was built around.

**Agentic Security Reviews**
Conducted 100+ cloud security reviews under Yahoo's Paranoid Security Review (PSR) program — partnering with the Product Security, Network, and Identity teams to threat-model and approve new cloud services and architectures before launch across Mail, Sports, Finance, and Central Tech, including third-party vendor integrations and AI/ML platform reviews. Designed and shipped the agentic SOAR-style review platform behind that throughput, eliminating a multi-week backlog. Built a cross-ticket intelligence layer from a large corpus of historical security review tickets — 1,700+ knowledge nodes across many security domains, technology stacks, and application profiles — wired into an autonomous Claude Code review agent with passive detection rules, slash commands, and bidirectional MCP integration with Jira and Confluence. Established as the team's standard review methodology.

**Autonomous Threat Intelligence Pipeline**
Autonomous 5-stage agentic pipeline (triage → analyze → decompose → peer review → synthesize) orchestrating 19 foundation models across 5 providers through a dynamic, performance-weighted allocation router that updates model assignments after each run. Output: vetted security initiative proposals from $1.40 per full sweep on metered pricing, the low end of the observed range. No single-model baseline run has been recorded, so no comparison figure is claimed.

**AI Security Operations Tooling**
- Security Ops Platform: FastAPI + Databricks SQL, dozens of API endpoints. Deterministic AI advisor trained on a large corpus of historical cloud security tickets for CSPM alert triage. 4-signal scoring model, confidence clamped 5–95%, hard deny gate for 6 critical baseline categories where auto-remediation is never appropriate. Adopted as team's primary operational workflow.
- Baseline Research Pipeline: Ingests 21 security intelligence feeds daily through 4-stage Claude orchestration (triage → analyze → draft → verify). CIS/NIST baseline discovery-to-draft in under 30 minutes at under $0.05/run. Processes 330+ items/day.
- Fleet-scale IaC policy-as-code coverage scanner written in Go, measuring Checkov adoption across the organization's entire repository estate.

**Force Multiplication**
Coached engineers on sister security teams on AI-assisted security engineering; distributed an AI security engineering toolkit (pre-commit security review, multi-perspective threat analysis) across the security organization. Pipeline architectures since adopted by other security teams.

## What Makes This Background Unusual

- Deep cloud identity expertise (IAM privilege escalation, CIEM, toxic combinations) combined with production AI systems engineering — not "uses AI tools," but ships multi-agent platforms with deterministic safety bounds (confidence clamping, hard deny gates, human-in-the-loop approval).
- Benchmark discipline: built the evaluation before trusting the tool (authored GOAT — 11 synthetic Terraform fixtures, 32 ground-truth findings — and evaluated the agent against all 32 before shipping).
- Small-team force multiplication: security coverage scaled through systems, not headcount, across one of the larger AWS/GCP estates operated by a team this size.

## Technical Stack

AWS, GCP, IAM, CIEM, CNAPP, CSPM, AI-SPM, Zero Trust, DevSecOps, Python, FastAPI, Databricks, Terraform, Amazon Bedrock, Vertex AI, Multi-Agent Orchestration, LLM Security, MCP, MITRE ATT&CK, Checkov, Docker, CIS Benchmarks, NIST CSF

Depth is uneven and worth stating. AWS security engineering, AWS IAM analysis, Python, and detection engineering are built. GCP and Azure are reviewed rather than built, and Azure is one substantial review, not a parallel to the other two. Containers are the managed non-Kubernetes scheduler: control authorship, task-role escalation paths, registry hygiene. Kubernetes is control authorship and architecture review; he has not operated a cluster in production.
